 Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves, Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Walker Kessler will start Friday’s game against the Warriors. 
 While Dončić is back after sitting out Wednesday’s win over the Clippers, Ziaire Williams will miss another game. As a result, LaRavia will remain in the starting lineup, while Dončić’s return pushes Quentin Grimes to the bench. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Another day, another injury report. Grant Liffmann and Chris Mannix examine the notable injuries to Jaren Jackson Jr., Kawhi Leonard, and the latest around Kristaps Porzingis' absence from the Warriors.

 Ziaire Williams 
 LAL

 Ziaire Williams (foot) is out for Friday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Williams will miss a second consecutive game with a left foot injury. Jake LaRavia started Wednesday’s win over the Clippers and will likely keep that role for Friday’s NBA Cup opener. 
 Ziaire Williams 
 LAL 
 Forward 
 #11 
 Ziaire Williams (foot) is questionable to play against the Warriors on Friday. 
 Williams missed Wednesday’s game, which resulted in Jake LaRavia starting and playing 35 minutes. LaRavia contributed 10 rebounds, three steals and two blocks and will likely head back to the bench if Williams is available to play. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić (back) is not on the injury report against the Warriors on Friday. 
 Dončić missed Wednesday’s game against the Clippers, which came on the second night of a back-to-back. He’ll be back to his usual spot in the starting lineup, which will likely push Quentin Grimes back to the bench following a productive spot start. 
 Quentin Grimes 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Austin Reaves, Quentin Grimes, Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Walker Kessler will start Wednesday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Luka Dončić and Ziaire Williams will miss Wednesday’s game, the Lakers’ second in as many nights. Grimes and LaRavia will replace them in the lineup, which also means Austin Reaves will take on the primary playmaking responsibilities for the starters. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić (back) has been ruled out against the Clippers on Wednesday. 
 Dončić will miss the second leg of the Lakers’ back-to-back, which means Austin Reaves should be the focal point of the offense. Quentin Grimes or Collin Sexton will likely replace Dončić in the starting unit, with both taking on extended roles. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić amassed 41 points (12-of-22 FGs, 11-of-13 Fts), five rebounds, nine assists, one block and six three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 One game removed from dropping 52 points on the Jazz, Dončić had another prolific scoring night on Tuesday. In addition to the high field-goal percentage, he kept the turnovers in check, committing only two. Despite averaging nearly six turnovers per game, Dončić has been one of the most valuable players in nine-cat formats. Shooting 87.5 percent from the foul line, which represents significant improvement, certainly helps. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Jazz with 52 points (17-of-30 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, two steals and eight three-pointers. 
 Dončić put on a show in Salt Lake City, recording his first 50-point game of the new season. And he was highly efficient, shooting well over 50 percent from the field. The only thing that could have made Sunday better for managers rostering Dončić was getting the two rebounds he needed to finish with a triple-double. The Lakers play four games in Week 2, starting Tuesday against the Trail Blazers. 
 Jake LaRavia 
 LAL 
 Forward 
 #12 
 Jake LaRavia (ankle) is off the injury report vs. Jazz. 
 LaRavia did not play on Friday against the Clippers, but was removed off the injury report ahead of Sunday’s tilt against the Jazz. The forward scored 10 points in 18 minutes of action in the Lakers season opener against the Warriors. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić tallied 23 points (8-of-21 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one block and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Clippers. 
 After an excellent start to his 2026-27 season against the Warriors on Wednesday, Dončić had some efficiency issues on Friday. While category league managers won’t be too concerned with the percentages, the Lakers’ point guard racked up a career-high 11 turnovers. By now, many managers rostering Dončić are fine with punting that category, but it’s still a startling number for him. He’ll look to put together a better showing when the Lakers visit the Jazz on Sunday. 
 Jake LaRavia 
 LAL 
 Forward 
 #12 
 Jake LaRavia (ankle) is out for Friday’s game against the Clippers. 
 LaRavia was initially listed as questionable, but it should be no surprise that he’s been ruled out Friday after he sprained his right ankle in Wednesday’s win over the Warriors. The good news is that the injury isn’t considered serious and he should return to game action soon. Without LaRavia, Quentin Grimes could see enough minutes off the bench to be worth steaming consideration in category leagues.

 Tari Eason got 11 points (4-of-12 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), 13 rebounds, two assists, and a steal in 26 minutes of play.
 After having a disappointing performance in the previous outing, he bounced back off the bench and really pulled down some rebounds. While he can put up a lot of numbers in a short amount of time, his ability to become a high level fantasy player on this team is limited as long as Kevin Durant and Jabari Smith Jr. are on this team.

 After playing a season-low 13 minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls, Bridges appeared to get the message on Friday. He matched his season-high with 12 points and added a few steals for good measure. Bridges’ fantasy value remains low, but Friday’s effort was a step in the right direction.

 Jalen Brunson finished Friday’s loss to the 76ers with 24 points (8-of-22 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, two steals and three three-pointers.
 Coming off his most efficient performance of the season in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls, Brunson cooled off against the 76ers. However, Brunson is shooting 39.5 percent from the field through six games, which is a big reason his current fantasy value isn’t matching preseason expectations.

 Kyrie Irving puts up 35 points (12-of-19 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, nine assists, and five 3-pointers in 116-111 win over the Rockets.
 kyrie is showing that he still has it despite missing the entire season last year. He likely won’t be as efficient or score that many points every game, but he’s been one of the most efficient scoring guards in NBA history. As long as the Mavericks keep winning, his place on this team becomes more and more secure.

 Karl-Anthony Towns tallied 22 points (8-of-15 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), 12 rebounds, three assists, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the 76ers.
 Towns has recorded a double-double in each of the Knicks’ six games this season, and he committed no fouls in Friday’s defeat. Given his occasional struggles with foul trouble, KAT avoiding it in a matchup with Philadelphia’s Joel Embiid is noteworthy. Unfortunately for managers rostering Towns, the Knicks don’t play again this week. But they do host the Nets on Monday.

 Cooper Flagg put on a show with 33 points (13-of-19 FGs, 7-of-10 FTs), nine rebounds, six assists, two steals, and a block in Mavericks win over the Rockets. 
 The Mavericks beat the undefeated Houston Rockets in this game and Flagg made the big time bucket to lead them to a win. He’s already one of the best players in fantasy basketball and there’s no sign of this slowing down. Getting him at the backend of the first round in many redraft leagues has turned into a massive steal at his ADP. Sit back and enjoy the ride if you have him.

 LeBron James put up 20 points (8-of-15 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), nine rebounds, eight assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Knicks.
 James made one of the game’s biggest plays, tipping in a Tyrese Maxey miss with 11.9 seconds remaining to extend the 76ers’ lead to five. That would be the final margin as Philadelphia moved to 5-1, and LeBron finished one rebound and two assists shy of a triple-double. At this stage in his career, the days of LeBron consistently providing robust stat lines are likely over. But he remains a valuable fantasy basketball player. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Anfernee Simons tallied 21 points (7-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Knicks.
 That’s two straight games of 20 points or more for Simons, who shot 5-of-8 from beyond the arc on Friday. While he remains a player who should be rostered in deep leagues at best, Simons’ performance against the Knicks was encouraging. Depending on who’s available, he may be worth a look for Saturday’s game against the Hornets.

 It was a very good performance from Gafford in this one despite being dunked on by Kevin Durant. It is notable that in the final couple minutes, he did roll his right ankle, was limping and was helped to the locker room. He did come back a minute later but it is something to monitor if he pops up on the injury report at some point.

 Franz Wagner with 26 points (8-of-18 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, eleven assists, a steal, two steals, and four turnovers on Friday. 
 The assists were a massive boost to his performance and should be a boost to your fantasy team, especially at this part of the week. With Paolo out, he has the opportunity to show what he can do, and see if there’s some untapped upside that he didn’t get to show with Paolo there. A lot of his upside will be dependent on the 3-point shot and he hasn’t shot it well up to this point in the season.
